FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Third Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Man-made Fibres, Cotton and their Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textiles Division 
Council. 


Lining fabrics are used for various apparels, such as blouses, frocks, coats, etc. It is Important that the lining fabric 
should withstand the treatments to which the apparels are exposed during actual use. Moreover, its durability 
should be comparable to that of the original apparel for which it is used. 


Lining cloth had been covered by three separate standards, namely, IS 2136 : 1974 “Specification for rayon вайп 
lining cloth (First Revision), IS 2228 : 1964 “Specification for rayon mix lining cloth (revision), and 
IS 7392 : 1974 ‘Specification for rayon taffeta lining cloth’. IS 2136 : 1974 was revised in 1988 incorporating 
IS 2228 : 1964 and IS 7392 : 1974. Subsequently IS 2228 : 1964 and IS 7392 : 1974 were superseded by 
IS 2136 : 1988. This standard is being revised again to incorporate the following changes: 


a) Method of test for count of yarn, end per dm, picks per dm, mass, blend composition, length and width 
has been specified; 


b) BIS certification marking clause has been modified; and 
c) References have been updated. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex D. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 2136 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


WOVEN FLAT LINING FABRICS FOR APPARELS — 
SPECIFICATION 


(Third Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard specifies the requirements for 
woven flat lining fabrics composed of man-made 
fibres or their blends with other fibres used for 
apparels. 


1.2 This specification is not applicable to woven 
pile, woven fusible, fire bonded fusible, sliver knit 
pile and sheepskin lining fabrics. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subjected to revision, and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of the standards. 


3 MANUFACTURE 

3.1 Yarn 

In case of lining fabrics made of man-made fibres or 
their blends, continuous filament yarn or spun yarn 


shall be used. The yarn shall be evenly and 
uniformly spun. 


3.2 Fabric 


The lining fabric shall be uniformly woven with firm 
selvedges and should be free from weaving and 
processing defects (see also Annex B). The 
constructional particulars of some important lining 
fabrics are given in Annex C for guidance only. 


4 REQUIREMENTS 


The flat woven lining fabrics for apparels shall 
conform to the requirements given in Table 1. The 
requirements of flammability and soil release 
efficiency in Table 1 are given as optional 
requirements and shall be applicable when an 
agreement has been reached between the buyer and 
the seller for these requirements. 


5 SEALED SAMPLE 


5.1 If in order to illustrate or specify certain 
characteristics, such as, general appearance, feel, 
shade of fabric a sample has been agreed upon and 
sealed, the supply shall be in conformity with the 
sample in such respects. 


5.1.1 The custody of the sealed sample shall be a 
matter of prior agreement between the buyer and the 
seller.

6 MARKING 


Each piece of fabric shall be marked on both ends 
with the following: 


a) Name of the material, namely, woven flat 
lining fabric for apparel; 

b) Nature and composition; 

с) Manufacturer's name, initials or trade 
mark; 

d) Month and year of manufacture; 


e) Dimensions (length and width) of the 
fabric; and 


f) Mass of fabric in g/m?.

6.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standard Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
product(s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


7 PACKING 


The cloth shall be packed in bales or cases in 
conformity with the procedure laid down either in IS 
2194 or in IS 2195 or as agreed between the buyer 
and the seller.

and weft yarn, number of ends and picks per 
decimetre, mass (g/m?), length and width of fabric

9 INSPECTION 


9.1 The fabric shall be inspected for serious and 
major flaws (see Annex B) and shall be considered 
as satisfactory if the following conditions are 
satisfied: 


a) Serious flaws: Nil 
b) Major flaws: 5 per 100 linear metres, Max 


9.1.1 All the defects shall be flagged by appropriate 
coloured threads on either of the selvedges. 


10 SAMPLING 
10.1 Lot 


The quantity of woven flat lining fabric purporting 


+ 2 percent units IS 3416 and IS 2005 

to be of one definite type and quality delivered to a 
buyer against one despatch note shall constitute a 
lot. 


NOTE — The sampling plan given in Table 2 shall give 
desired protection to the buyer and the seller provided the 
lot submitted for inspection is homogeneous. To ensure 
homogeneity of the lot it is recommended to follow the 
method given in IS 4905. 


10.2 The conformity of the lot to the requirements 
of this standard shall be adjudged on the basis of the 
tests carried out on the samples selected from it. 


10.3 Unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer 
and the seller, the number of pieces to be selected 
from a lot shall be in accordance with col (1) and 
col (2) of Table 3.

ANNEX B 


(Clauses 3.2 and 9.1) 
CATEGORIZATION OF FLAWS 


В-1 SERIOUS FLAWS 


B-1.1 The serious flaws include: 


a) 


b) 


8) 
h) 


j) 


One or more ends missing in the body of 
the material throughout its length, or more 
than three ends missing at a place and 
running over 600 mm or prominently 
noticeable double end running throughout 
the length of the piece; 

Undressed snarls noticeable over a length 
exceeding 3 percent of the length of the 
piece; 

Bad smashes definitely rupturing the 
texture of the fabric; 

Holes, cut or tear; 

Reed marks prominently noticeable over a 
length exceeding 5 percent of the length of 
the piece; 

Defective or damaged selvedge noticeable 
over a length exceeding 5 percent of the 
length of the piece; 

Very large floats; 

Missing weft across full width for more 
than 6 mm; and 

Mechanical damage, abrasion marks 
affecting the strength of the fabric. 


8-2 MAJOR FLAWS 


8.2.1 The major flaws include: 


a) 


Weft crack or two or more missing picks 
less than 6 mm across the width of the 
fabric; 


b) 


с) 


d) 


e) 


Weft bar due to the difference in raw 
material, count, twist, lustre, colour, shade 
or pick spacing of adjacent groups of weft 
yarns; 

More than two adjacent ends running 
parallel or broken or missing end extending 
beyond 100 mm; 

Noticeable warp or weft floats over 6.5 mm 
square or if over 13 mm long or broad, 
floating over more than four threads; 


Noticeable oil or other stains in the fabric 
unless the causes are known and the effects 
are known to be harmless; 


Prominently noticeable slub; 
Conspicuous broken pattern; 


Gout due to foreign matter, usually lint or 
waste, woven into the fabrics; 


Hard inclusions; 
Badly made pull backs; 


Prominent selvedge defects, that 15, weak, 
slack, wavy, tight or scalloped selvedge; 


Significant shading or listing in fabrics 
having a gradual change in tone or depth of 
shade of fabric (excluding selvedge or 
border running parallel to the selvedge); 


Coloured flecks; 

Blurred or dark patch; 

Patchy, streaky or uneven dyeing; 

Dye bar; 

Printing defect which mars the general 
appearance of the fabric; and 


Longitudinal bars of relatively tight or slack 
warp threads.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
